chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed and High: 'but whoever is driven to necessity, not rebelling, nor exceeding the limit.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The rebel is the one who rises against the Imam, and the transgressor is the one who cuts off the road (bandit); the dead meat is not permissible to him.'

key_terms.الْإِمَام: The Imam, the religious and political leader
key_terms.الْبَاغِي: The rebel, specifically one who rises against the Imam
key_terms.الْعَادِي: The transgressor, specifically one who cuts off the road (bandit)
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةُ: Dead meat (animal that died without ritual slaughter)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the rebel and the transgressor in the context of eating dead meat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the conditions of 'dharurah' (necessity) by distinguishing between general transgression and specific political or social crimes, identifying 'al-baghi' as rebellion against the Imam and 'al-'adi' as highway robbery. It establishes that while necessity generally permits the forbidden, the permissibility is forfeited if the individual's excess involves these distinct categories of wrongdoing, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the link between legal status and moral conduct. This interpretation underscores the authority of the Imam in defining the limits of permissible deviation from divine law.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from the one who mentioned it,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Blessed and High [2:173] but whoever is driven to necessity, not rebelling, nor exceeding the limit. Heasws said: ‘The rebel is one who comes out against the Imamasws, and the transgressor is the one who cuts-off the road (bandit); the dead not being Permissible to him’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Blessed, most High, ‘Those who are compelled without being rebels or transgressors . . [2:172]
He (the Imam) said, ‘A rebel is one who rises against the Imam and a transgressor is one who cuts off the road and dead animals are not lawful for him.”’
